_comment: Eastern Cape Department of Education Grade 10 Mathematical Literacy P1, November 2019 provincial common examination.
Questions and marking-guideline answers extracted from the text layer of the official PDFs
(paper1.pdf, paper1_memo.pdf) and read against the rendered pages. Mathematical
Literacy questions hang off shared scenario boxes: the scenario (tables, graphs, plans and maps
described in bracketed words) is the 'context' of the first sub-question of each block and applies
to the sub-questions after it. memo_answer gives the guideline's working and final answer with
decimal commas kept; the guideline's mark codes (M method, A accuracy, CA consistent accuracy, RT
reading from table, C conclusion, O opinion, S simplification, R rounding) and level tags are left out.
FORMAT: 75 marks, 1½ hours, five compulsory questions (Q1 15, Q2 20, Q3 10, Q4 12, Q5 18).

subject: Mathematical Literacy

questions.context: QUESTION 1 | The fundraising committee of your school is planning their annual Spring Dance. They decided on a venue that charges R7 500,00 for a function of five hours, with an additional charge of R900,00 per hour, or part thereof. The venue accommodates 120 guests for a three-course meal and dancing.
questions.text: Identify the value that represents the fixed amount.
questions.topic: Patterns and relationships: tariff tables and graphs

questions.text: Is the number of guests attending the dance, discrete or continuous data?
questions.topic: Data handling: collecting, organising and summarising data

questions.text: If 45% of the people attending the dance are males, calculate the number of males at the dance.
questions.memo_answer: Number of males = 120 x 45% = 120 x 0,45 = 54 males

questions.context: 1.4 The dance starts at 18:30 and ends at 23:55.
questions.text: Determine the duration of the dance, in hours and minutes.
Hence, calculate the cost of the venue for 120 guests.
questions.topic: Patterns and relationships: tariff tables and graphs

questions.text: Calculate the average amount each guest will pay for the three-course meal and dance.
The dance floor is a square in the middle of the room, with a side length of 6 m. Calculate the perimeter of the dance floor. You may use the formula: Perimeter = 4 × side

questions.context: QUESTION 2 | 2.1 Study TABLE 1 below regarding bank fees at Mega Bank and answer the questions that follow. [TABLE 1: BANK FEES FOR MEGA BANK ACCOUNT. Monthly account fee R65,00; Cellphone banking R0,00; Cash withdrawals (Mega Bank ATM): first R1 500 R0,00, more than R1 500 R12,00 + R1,20 per R100 (or part thereof); Cash withdrawals (other bank ATM) R15,00.]
questions.text: What is the monthly fee of having this account?
Ababalwe withdraws R1 700 at a Mega Bank ATM. Calculate what this withdrawal will cost her.
Ababalwe had to transfer R500 to her mother’s account. She decided to use her cellphone banking to do this. How much did this transaction cost her?
While at the mall, Ababalwe had lunch at a restaurant. Her bill, excluding VAT, was R90,80. Calculate the amount of VAT that will be charged, if VAT is calculated at 15%.
questions.topic: Finance: VAT, discount and simple interest

questions.text: Ababalwe invests R2 000 into a fixed deposit account, for a period of two years. The bank offers her simple interest at a rate of 9,5% p.a. Calculate the value of her investment after two years.
questions.memo_answer:
Interest per year = R2 000 x 0,095 = R190
Total interest = R190 x 2 = R380
Total value = R2 000 + R380 = R2 380

questions.context: 2.4 TABLE 2 below shows a rough statement of Bane's income and expenditure items for a month. Study the table and answer the questions that follow. [TABLE 2: INCOME AND EXPENDITURE FOR BANE. Income: Salary R11 750. Expenditure: Groceries R2 100; Rent ---; Petrol R1 000; Car payment R1 800; Electricity ---; Clothing R450; Insurance R320; Entertainment R600.]
questions.text: Name ONE variable and ONE fixed expenditure item.
questions.memo_answer:
Variable (choose ONE): groceries, petrol, electricity, clothing, entertainment
Fixed (choose ONE): rent, car payment, insurance

questions.text: Bane spends a total of R3 700 on electricity and rent combined. If the ratio of electricity to rent is 1 : 4, determine the amount she pays for electricity.
questions.memo_answer:
Total = 1 + 4 = 5 parts
Electricity = 1/5 x R3 700 = R740

questions.text: Calculate what percentage Bane’s groceries is of her salary. Round your answer off to the nearest percentage.

questions.context: QUESTION 3 | Given below is a simple floor plan of a one-bedroom flat. Study the plan and answer the questions that follow. The floor plan is not drawn to scale. [Floor plan: a kitchen/living room on the left (west) side with the front door in its west wall, a bedroom with a double bed top-centre, and a bathroom (bath, basin, toilet, shower) on the right; windows drawn as narrow rectangles - two on the north wall, one on the east wall of the bathroom, one on the west wall and one on the south wall of the living room; north arrow points up. Key: window, door.]
questions.text: How many windows does this flat have?
questions.topic: Maps and plans: scale, floor plans and elevation plans

questions.text: From which general direction would you be entering the flat, if you came in at the front door in the living room?
questions.topic: Maps and plans: scale, floor plans and elevation plans

questions.context: 3.3 The living room/kitchen is going to be tiled. The scale used for this plan is 1 : 50.
questions.text: Explain the meaning of the scale 1 : 50.
questions.topic: Maps and plans: scale, floor plans and elevation plans
questions.memo_answer: One unit on the floor plan is equal to fifty units in reality.

questions.text: If the width on the plan measures 4,8 cm and the length measures 9,3 cm, calculate the real area of the room. Give your answer in square metres (m2). You may use the formula: Area = length × breadth
questions.topic: Maps and plans: scale, floor plans and elevation plans
questions.memo_answer:
Real width: 4,8 cm x 50 = 240 cm = 2,4 m
Real length: 9,3 cm x 50 = 465 cm = 4,65 m
Area = 2,4 m x 4,65 m = 11,16 m²

questions.context: QUESTION 4 | Given below is a simple cheese and tomato pizza recipe. Study the recipe and answer the questions that follow. SIMPLE CHEESE AND TOMATO PIZZA (makes 1 large pizza): ¾ cup homemade pizza dough; 1 tbsp olive oil; 2 cloves garlic; 75 mℓ tomato paste; 0,23 kg mozzarella cheese; 2 tomatoes; salt and pepper to taste. Remember: 1 cup = 250 mℓ; 1 tablespoon = 15 mℓ; 1 teaspoon = 5 mℓ.
questions.text: Determine the amount of homemade pizza dough needed for 3 large pizzas. Give your answer in millilitres (mℓ).
How many tablespoons of tomato paste is needed for this recipe?
Convert the amount of cheese to grams.

questions.context: 4.4 When the pizza is completed, the base has a diameter of 32 cm and a height of 12 mm. [Picture of a pizza labelled Diameter = 32 cm, Height = 12 mm.]
questions.text: Write down the radius of one pizza base.
questions.memo_answer:
Radius = 32 cm ÷ 2 = 16 cm
OR radius = 320 mm ÷ 2 = 160 mm

questions.text: Calculate the volume of one pizza (in mm³). You may use the formula: Volume = π r² x h; where π = 3,142
questions.memo_answer:
Volume = 3,142 x (160 mm)² x 12 mm = 965 222,4 mm³
OR volume = 3,142 x (16 cm)² x 1,2 cm = 965,2224 cm³ ≈ 965 222,4 mm³

questions.context: QUESTION 5 | 5.1 A group of Grade 10 learners were asked what amount of airtime they use in a month. The results are given in the table below. [TABLE 3: RESULTS OF GRADE 10 AIRTIME USAGE SURVEY: R12, R29, R5, R5, R12, R29, R29, R110, R5, R5, R12, R29, R29, R55, R5, R12.]
questions.text: Define the term median.
questions.topic: Data handling: collecting, organising and summarising data
questions.memo_answer: The median is the middle value of a data set after arranging it in ascending/descending order.

questions.text: Determine the mode for the above data.
questions.topic: Data handling: collecting, organising and summarising data

questions.text: Calculate the average amount of airtime used by the learners in a month.
questions.topic: Data handling: collecting, organising and summarising data

questions.text: Show by means of calculation that the range of this data is R105.
questions.topic: Data handling: collecting, organising and summarising data

questions.text: What is the probability that a learner uses R29 airtime in a month? Give your answer as a decimal fraction, rounded off to three decimal places.

questions.context: 5.2 A survey was conducted where learners were asked what their favourite brand of sneakers is. The results are shown in the figure below. [Pie chart FAVOURITE SNEAKERS with five sectors: A (largest), C, D, B and E (smallest). Key: A Adidas; B Reebok; C Nike; D Puma; E Converse.]
questions.text: Name the type of graph illustrated above.
questions.topic: Data handling: representing and analysing graphs

questions.text: Name the THREE most favourite brands of sneakers.
questions.topic: Data handling: representing and analysing graphs
questions.memo_answer: Adidas, Nike, Puma OR A, C, D

questions.text: If 300 learners were involved in the survey, and 32% preferred Adidas sneakers, calculate the number of learners who favoured Adidas.
